body:
# Post-v0.6.5 requirement reconciliation — prevent omitted scope and duplicate work

**Owner directive, 2026-11-05:** Last AQUORA release missed a major second-visualizer redesign despite successful v0.6.5 software publication. Audit ALL previously requested tasks, especially deferred work, and make the next build reject unexplained omissions. Preserve accepted v0.6.5 software/installer, and respect exclusive build ownership.

## Verified root cause
- v0.6.5 accepted scope explicitly covered only **Issues #2, #16, #24, #26–#30 and draft PR #25**, see `validation/integration-065/REQUIREMENTS.md`. That does NOT include Issue #17's latest ground-up water/sand cymatics replacement brief.
- The repo's `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` then reported "no outstanding v0.6.5 software implementation" without a next-release carry-forward queue.
- 30 issues remained open (and 0 closed) as of the audit; some of these are software-complete and others deferred, partially implemented, or pending hardware aesthetic/listening checks. An unqualified open/closed flag is insufficient.
- Current main `device/visual_worker.c` still uses a **17×17 nodal field and up to 256 marching contour segments** in `resonance_job()`; `device/ui.c::visual_name()` still displays **Resonance Plate**. This is not the owner's requested distinct, organic water/sand system in [#17](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/17#issuecomment-6667383022). CPU-cost reductions in #26 do not count as completing #17.

## Current release scope — latest owner-authorized deferral

Approval: https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/31#issuecomment-6702097918 and https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/issues/32#issuecomment-6702099240. This supersedes earlier USB-required wording.

| Requirement ID | v0.6.6 disposition | Carry-forward / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| MIDI-USB | OWNER-AUTHORIZED DEFERRED / not a release blocker | Revisit after KIRA-9 has a good working firmware build and owner reprioritizes. Preserve partial code; do not enable unfinished performance routing. |
| MIDI-BLE | OWNER-AUTHORIZED DEFERRED / not a release blocker | Same follow-up trigger; no pairing, scanning or MIDI radio ownership in this release. |
| MIDI-AIR | REQUIRED | Functional AIR, internal playback, firmware update SysEx and internal-tempo PLAY LED remain required. |

All non-MIDI software acceptance, backups and publication gates remain mandatory. External MIDI clock/routing/interoperability acceptance is deferred with the transports. Preserve v0.6.5 and all completed work; KIRA-9 untouched.

## Reconciled queue — v0.6.6 software delivered (historical brief below)
- **P0 CONFIRMED MISSED:** #17 genuine ground-up second visualizer replacement: visible water ripples/standing-wave vibration and sand-like granular migration and settling along stable nodes, visibly distinct from Resonance Plate/Polar Bloom; accurate music onset, pitch, intention, frequency, silence and morph response; preview sequences for low/high notes, silence, formation, settling, transitions; owner aesthetic acceptance **UNVERIFIED**. No "cosmetic contour redesign" accepted. Prevent regression to 58ms draw/6ms geometry; render bounded, audio-first, native + forced-single-core fallback and measured host comparisons. User specifically forbids either visualizer on the public showcase gallery; keep branded spiral intro separate.
- **OWNER-AUTHORIZED DEFERRED:** #31 performance USB and BLE MIDI, per the current-scope matrix above; AIR remains required.
- **P1/P0 SUBJECT TO VERIFICATION:** #13 AIR usability (true packet/proximity feedback, accessible effect routing, no fake scanning), #18 muffled drum-kit owner listening findings, #9 fresh intention A→B→A variation incl unlocked patch IDs/evolution over sessions; consult latest source/tests and hardware observations before assuming a missing implementation. Do not override an already-proven fix.
- **EVIDENCE GAPS / targeted audit, not blanket rebuild:** #1 LED On (source now sets `all_keys`, physical matrix still unverified); #3 intention/style-aware Nature AUTO/MANUAL/OFF; #4 real SOUND/EVOLVE graphs and website APNG; #5 realistic Birds/Forest; #10 fullscreen frame occupancy; #19 website deployment (live publication json reports current site); #20 SAVE one-press; #21 visual themes; #22 v0.6.4 catch-all; #23 music modes + automatic glide/vibrato. Also inspect any other unresolved owner comments. Classify each as **Software completed / Partial / Blocked / Owner hardware unverified / Open** with evidence. Do not conflate a physical listening claim with a software test.
- **Already accepted software:** #2, #16 scoped typography/themes, #24, #26–#30 as specifically recorded in v0.6.5 acceptance; do not reimplement without concrete regression evidence. This does NOT waive remaining #16 subrequirements or physical acceptance.

## Mandatory prevention system — applies to both AQUORA and KIRA-9
1. Before build, generate a **single current requirement register** from root scope, active queue, every open issue and **latest owner comments** (including deferred issues and changes after previous release). One canonical ID for each distinct feature; deduplicate aliases while preserving all acceptance conditions.
2. Each requirement row: ID, current owner wording + source URL/comment, version introduced/targeted, priority, status (NEW / PARTIAL / COMPLETED SOFTWARE / BLOCKED / OWNER-UNVERIFIED), exact source file/function/commit, targeted automated test IDs, emulated visual/audio artifacts, physical test owner and explicit **carry-forward disposition**.
3. **Release blockers**: no unclassified issue/owner comment; no P0 row silently deferred; no row marked completed based on notes, code existing, mock tests, a rename or successful compilation alone. Design-heavy visual work requires before/after true 240×240 sequences with representative scenarios reviewed against the *latest* requested visual goal, not merely geometric-count or hash changes.
4. At end, compare planned vs actually delivered; **zero unexplained missing requirements**. For genuine deferral, record owner's accepted scope decision, explicit next version, current blocking rationale, and a visible NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE entry. A successful hotfix is not permission to declare the entire project backlog empty.
5. Compact `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` holds ONLY unfinished work, each with an ID/link; archive completed with source/test/release evidence in `CHANGELOG.md` / `validation/`. Synchronize GitHub issue states/comments as appropriate; don't blindly close issues with owner hardware checks pending.
6. Release gate script/CI should validate requirement IDs and traceability file: fail on missing status, missing P0 evidence, falsely completed items without commits/tests, incomplete carry-forward or stale release version. Add targeted negative test proving a deliberately deferred requirement fails if missing from the next queue.
7. Respect project-specific exclusive build lock, no overlapping writers/publishers, versioned verified remote backups before tests and interruptions, rebuild only changed/regression-affected tests, one continuous end-to-end workflow and no repeated "proceed" requests. Publish only after software acceptance. Hardware tests remain user-performed and truthfully labeled UNVERIFIED.

**Status: v0.6.6 SOFTWARE COMPLETE AND PUBLISHED; OWNER HARDWARE/AESTHETIC CHECKS OPEN.**

All 45 requirement rows and 74 owner comments are classified in [the canonical register](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/aquora-next-integration/validation/next-requirements.json), with source commits, targeted tests/artifacts and carry-forward dispositions. The historical brief above is preserved for traceability; it is not an instruction to rebuild accepted work.

| Release gate | Evidence / result |
|---|---|
| Non-MIDI software acceptance | [Run 42353932681](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/actions/runs/42353932681) PASS; reuses matching native/repro/single-core and seven direct updater paths without unnecessary rebuilds. |
| Exact release publication | [v0.6.6](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/releases/tag/v0.6.6), target 295c1d1d489cd9b7a0b87ea797031d39ee673fe4; [publisher](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/actions/runs/42357005353) PASS. |
| Backups | All 11 public assets independently downloaded and SHA256 checked; download ZIP internal manifest/CRC and independent publisher backup agree. [Verification](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/aquora-next-integration/validation/release-066/BACKUP_VERIFICATION.json). a3f1b13 exact tree preserved at 9a0ce93; partial MIDI tree on aquora-preserved-midi-82ca1f1. |
| Installer / website | [Live installer](https://parallax8-studio.jminie66.chatgpt.site/install/), Site v184; real HTTPS WASM and Studio controls verified. [Pages mirror](https://codingslapfu.github.io/AQUORA/install/), deployment 42357397911 PASS. |
| Physical / subjective checks | OWNER-UNVERIFIED: FM-1 flash/update/rollback, actual FPS/XRUN/audio headroom/soak, RF/AIR sensitivity, physical brightness, listening balance and visual aesthetics. These are not claimed as measured on-device. |

MIDI-USB and MIDI-BLE remain **OWNER-AUTHORIZED DEFERRED, not release blockers**. No exposed performance MIDI; AIR/internal playback/clock/update SysEx retained. Revisit only after KIRA-9 has a good working firmware build and owner reprioritizes. [Active queue](https://github.com/CodingSlapfu/AQUORA/blob/aquora-next-integration/NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md). No KIRA-9 files changed. Prior releases/backups preserved.

title: P0 next build: eight-role arrangement evolution, fading entrances/exits and inactive mixer tracks
body:
## Owner-reported hardware observation — November 6, 2026

While watching the MIXER on the latest AQUORA firmware, the owner sees that **all eight tracks never seem to be used**: some tracks appear disabled, unassigned, or never generate audio over the entire listening period. This is an observational report, **not yet a verified root cause**. The latest build otherwise runs smoothly with no lag observed so far; protect that performance baseline.

## Required next-build investigation and fix

1. Audit the **eight intended musical roles, including drums**, their patch/kit assignment, generated phrases and evolution, and mixer track/bus mapping. Confirm whether all eight are configured, enabled, and capable of contributing in the default arrangement. Distinguish genuinely silent source roles from non-role buses and intentionally sparse musical rests.
2. Trace each role across generator selection -> note scheduling -> voices/voice stealing -> envelopes/FX -> gains/mute/solo/Auto Level/Auto Gain -> mixer meters -> DAC. Look for permanently empty/unassigned patches, zero gain, mute defaults, routing/channel mismatches, low priority voices, and UI meters that falsely imply inactivity.
3. Exercise **13 intentions × three music modes**, and **16/32/64** step loops, New Song, Reroll Sounds, Freeze/evolution, save/recall, STOP/PLAY, and intentional sparse arrangements. Ensure each role expected by the design becomes meaningfully active over a long enough interval, with musical variation and without mandatory eight-part continuous playback.
4. Add targeted role-activity diagnostics: per-role patch ID, enabled/mute/solo state, generated-event count, accepted voice count, post-gain signal level/peak and mixer meter identity. In automated renders, inspect both event counts and actual audible PCM per-role stems / sampled mix; distinguish silence caused by intentional arrangement from failure.
5. Fix proven defects **without** forcing all eight roles to sound in every bar, muddying arrangements, artificially inflating meters, increasing CPU/XRUNs, or regressing the owner's currently smooth v0.6.5 audio/UI performance.
6. Supply source+test evidence and before/after diagnostics, plus a short owner hardware acceptance checklist showing how to verify all eight roles on the FM-1 mixer. Mark physical confirmation **OWNER-UNVERIFIED** until tested.

**Priority:** P0 core generative audio role/track integrity for next build. Carry forward in `NEXT_BUILD_ACTIVE.md` and requirement matrix Issue #32. Do not modify published v0.6.5 assets as part of this backlog note.

## Additional owner hardware feedback — dynamic track entrances/exits (2026-11-06)

Owner clarification: a generated song **typically uses the same ~4–5 musical tracks for the entire listening session**; those parts persist, while remaining roles stay silent from start to finish. The desired experience is a living arrangement: **different roles should gradually enter and leave as the song evolves**, with audible, smooth fade-ins and fade-outs rather than a fixed set of channels throughout the song.

### Acceptance criteria (added to existing P0 issue)

- Implement or verify a phrase-/section-level **role-activity plan** for all eight intended musical roles (including drums): rotate supporting parts in/out over time while retaining harmonic coherence, intention/style, recognizability and musical flow. Evolution should be perceptible across **16/32/64-step loops** and longer sessions.
- Support smoothly automated **per-role fade-in/fade-out envelopes** and appropriate transitions/crossfades on phrase or section boundaries (click-free, avoid abrupt re-entry, note tails/reverb handled gracefully); protect the audio-thread budget. Preserve musical rests and occasional intentionally sparse passages; **do not force eight simultaneous loud tracks**.

This is a **requested next-build behavior**, not an implemented fix or evidence that the current generator is broken in a particular subsystem. Do not start a separate concurrent build or modify the current released firmware for this note.


## Owner clarification — musical discretion, not eight-track quota

All eight roles are **available**, but **they do not all need to play in the same song, at once, or even during one entire song**. The style, selected intention, chord/harmonic progression, musical phrases and evolving arrangement should organically determine which instruments enter, overlap, fade, depart, or remain silent. A beautiful sparse piece might use only a few. Some styles or evolutions may genuinely call for all eight. The failure to investigate is **permanently unavailable/nonfunctional roles or an unintentionally static 4–5-track configuration**, not a requirement to force every role into every composition. No arbitrary minimum-track quota or rotation timer. Test all eight roles' capability in suitable contexts and the musical appropriateness of transitions.

SIREN demonstrates style-weighted forms and section-aware note gating; its code does **not** demonstrate the desired continuous eight-role crossfade system, which AQUORA must design independently. ## Owner scope revision — 2026-11-07 (supersedes earlier "improve/replace Cymatics Mode 2" interpretation)

**KEEP the existing v0.6.6 second visualizer, _Cymatics_, exactly as a selectable mode.** Owner likes its appearance, **especially on a black background**, and does **not** want its artistic identity replaced by Chladni/mandala patterns. Build a **NEW THIRD, distinct visualizer mode**, provisionally named **Chladni** (or **Chladni Mandala**, name subject to owner's final preference).

### Three modes, not a replacement
1. **Original** — preserve existing stock/Original visualizer fidelity and its character.
2. **Cymatics** — preserve the current v0.6.6 water/sand mode and particularly its black-background appearance, existing water feel and smoothness. Any shared improvements must be non-destructive and independently reviewed.
3. **NEW: Chladni** — visually distinct, explicitly music-reactive vibrating-plate/sand nodal figures and elegant geometric/mandala-like forms.

### Third-mode requirements
- **True audible post-gain reactivity:** energetic transient response (including audible drums), pitch/harmonics influencing modal geometry, bass swelling and release, meaningful loud/quiet differences; avoid decorative random animation disconnected from sound.
- **Chladni nodal behavior:** thin sand-like particles gather on still nodal lines as vibrating regions change; recognizable cross, line, radial/spoke, ring, petal, starburst, rosette, symmetric polygon and snowflake-inspired mode families, with coherent shifts based on the musical source. No scientific-fidelity or mystical-frequency claims.
- **Geometry:** evolving, intricate mandala-like symmetrical arrangements formed by modal basis/interference and particle flow, rather than merely drawing canned shapes. Harmonies/interference can cause richer superpositions and transitions.
- **Fluid motion and calm:** beat/attack pulses are visible, sustained sound maintains a living pattern, pitch changes morph smoothly, and silence allows water/particles to settle naturally. Remain artistically consistent with AQUORA's sound-healing ambience.
- **Resource budget:** same performance-first 240×240, audio-priority graphics constraints as v0.6.6; avoid FFT or heavy audio-thread math; bounded stable renderer, DMA safety, measured frame times, no regression to v0.6.5 lag/XRUN, preserve real-world 0.6.6 smoothness and single-core fallback.
- **Selector, save/load, migration:** Existing firmware uses **binary `visual_mode` state** (e.g. `device/app.c` `visual_mode=d>0` and `settings.visual<=1`). Redesign as 3 explicit choices with on-screen name/preview, deterministic selection and backward-compatible migration of 0=Original, 1=Cymatics (no accidental changes to existing preferences). Include fullscreen/idle startup settings, visualizer persistence, host controls, emulator and website parity. Prevent changing source mode by unrelated controls.
- **Theme behavior:** Mode 3 must look good on both black and white themes. The *cross-mode white background visibility problem* is tracked separately in #37; don't overfit visuals just by forcing a dark canvas.
- **Validation:** Actual 240×240 animations for lead/bass/drums, chord onsets, pitch sweeps, loud/quiet, mode morph/settle, silence, frequency changes, white and black themes. Test all three modes, selection/persistence/migration, audio-first FPS/XRUN, delayed-DMA and single-core fallback. Owner aesthetic and real hardware acceptance remain unverified until physical testing.

This is **new post-v0.6.6 scope**. Preserve existing published v0.6.6 packages, tests, repositories and installers; no unapproved code edits or parallel builders. Both USB and BLE performance MIDI remain explicitly deferred; KIRA-9 untouched.

title: Next AQUORA P0: All three visualizers must respond strongly to internal music even when physical master volume is zero
body:
## Owner physical FM-1 request — Nov 7, 2026 — all modes, including master level zero

> "all visualizer should react much more to the audio, and even [if] the volume is set to 0."

This is an explicit **cross-mode** requirement: **Original** (Mode 1), preserved **Cymatics** (Mode 2) and planned **Chladni** (Mode 3, #36) must show substantially clearer, musically meaningful motion. **Turning the FM-1's physical master volume knob all the way to zero must NOT stop or suppress visualization while the AQUORA transport/audio engine is still producing music internally.** Visually silent != acoustically muted.

### Exact audio signal contract (avoid false triggers)
- Drive visual animation using **internal pre-physical-master / pre-speaker-output** signal telemetry: audio energy / RMS, transient/onset strength, per-role audible contributions, harmonic/pitch context and optional spectral proxies from the engine **before hardware master attenuation**. Preserve proper **post-track/solo/arrangement-gain** semantics: a muted or inactive role should not create fictitious "audible" visual peaks; external audio if actually routed through engine can be included when available. Effective internal mix can still animate while headphone/speaker output is muted.
- Physical master **0% vs 100%** for the same sequence should yield **equivalent visual motion** (apart from nondeterministic capture timing), despite exactly muted DAC output at 0%. This behavior should also hold during smooth changes of master while running and after saved preferences reload.
- No "visualization from the absolute constant animation clock only": rhythmic kicks should induce conspicuous but controlled impulses, bass should cause slower/heavier waves, melody pitches should affect motion/geometry, chords should generate coherent interference; quiet passages should be visibly calmer, and attack/decay should be observable. Keep the artistically distinct identities of the three modes.
- When **STOP** is pressed or engine genuinely silent, visual activity should **decay/settle naturally**, not keep showing full-volume musical excitation. Intentional reference/binaural/Nature layers may animate only when truly active internally. Preserve ongoing ambient ease; avoid frantic strobing / flicker and false “frequency healing” claims.
- Respect user-selected black/white background and improved white-theme contrast requirement #37. Preserve particularly the current **Cymatics Mode 2** black-background appearance, not replace it with Mode 3's nodal mandalas.
- Avoid additional DSP/heavy analysis in the real-time audio callback. Reuse existing pre-master track meters, `engine.master_peak`, role/onset/pitch telemetry as safe inputs or add lightweight bounded snapshots; use frame-domain smoothing/attack-release and separate geometry/render work, not FFT or costly sample-by-sample graphics.

### Current source grounding (v0.6.6)
- `device/app.c::app_render(...,master)` applies physical master in `output_gain` **after** `sr_render(&engine,pcm,n)`. The internal mix/telemetry therefore need not be tied to hardware master, but must be verified through end-to-end tests.
- `device/visual_worker.c::prepare_geometry()` samples `engine.tracks[t].meter`, role onset/events, pitch and engine frequency; `visual_job` uses meter to set Original petal radius and `resonance_job` uses meter/onset to drive Cymatics water/sand. They may need **higher perceptual dynamic range**, more transient response and more meaningful musical differentiation without driving overload.
- Do not fake a full audio response simply by cranking up static `energy` or decorative phase, nor derive visual amplitude from the post-hardware-master `lr[]` output buffer.

### Acceptance criteria and evidence
1. Deterministic/recorded **same internally generated musical sequence** at physical master 0, low, and high: output PCM muted at zero, yet per-frame visual telemetry and geometric reaction demonstrably equivalent. Also move master dynamically during PLAY; no discontinuity in visual response.
2. Contrast clips: kick/snare/percussion transients, solo bass swell/glide, lead notes, chord/polyphony, changing pitch & harmonies, loud-vs-soft, Nature-only, intentional silence, STOP and release tails. Every mode must show strong **observable correlations to music** and reasonable decay; no permanently animated noisy screen while truly stopped.
3. Validate all three modes in black/white themes and full-screen/PLAY; 240×240 genuine renderer captures/short animations for comparison, owner aesthetic approval pending physical device test.
4. Keep v0.6.6 smoothness and audio-first priority: host/native/forced-single-core tests, instrument frame p95/p99, FPS/XRUN safety, DMA ownership; robust fallback if load high. No additional full-screen redraw per sample, preserve battery and display responsiveness.
5. Record required traceability in #32 matrix and active queue; **this is new post-v0.6.6 scope**. Preserve published release/tag/installer; do not restart an active build, do not modify KIRA-9; USB/BLE performance MIDI remain owner-authorized deferred.

Related: #17 (Cymatics retained), #33 (Original FPS/fidelity), #36 (third Chladni), #37 (white-theme contrast), #35 (SOUND/SELECT UI regression).

## Owner hardware behavior request — AQUORA next build (2026-11-07)

**Expected:** "Next build for AQUORA should remember some basic things on shutoff, like which visualizer you selected." This must also work if the user changes the visualizer **while music is playing** and subsequently powers off without pressing STOP.

### Scope — global device preferences, separate from a musical arrangement
- **MUST persist the chosen visualizer** through physical power-off/reboot. With the planned three modes (#36), preserve exact indices and names `0=Original`, `1=Cymatics`, `2=Chladni`, and transparently migrate prior two-mode v0.6.6 preferences `0/1` without changing the user's selection.
- Persist other **global usability preferences** consistent with pre-existing settings (chosen white/black background, theme, font/size, frame-policy preference, LED mode/brightness preference where supported, AIR mapping preferences and startup sound option), without conflating them with momentary song parameters. Do not add broad indiscriminate writes; verify each preference has intentional save/load semantics.
- **Do not persist automatic live drum/FX arrangement values as global device preferences.** User explicitly wants drum settings to initialize from suitable defaults at reboot and to be chosen automatically **when an intention/music style is selected** (#40). Four saved arrangement banks are independent and must restore their explicitly saved song states when the user chooses a bank.
- Avoid banking side effects: **loading/saving/replacing a bank must not unexpectedly overwrite the globally preferred visualizer** unless the user explicitly chooses to restore a bank's visual setting. Current `device/arrangement.c::arrangement_apply` sets `visual_mode=record->visual`; document and correct precedence.
- Preferences should survive an abrupt ordinary device off after a recent edit (within an explicitly bounded commit window) **without requiring the user to stop PLAY** or perform an undiscoverable save. Provide visible confirmation such as brief "Preference saved" when meaningful; no excessive indicator clutter.

### Source audit — v0.6.6
- `device/app.c::save_preferences` includes `settings.visual=visual_mode`, and `app_init` restores it *after* `arrangement_init` resets visual index. A formal persistence path exists.
- `device/app.c::app_frame` schedules `save_preferences()` only when `!engine.running&&!requested_play&&!engine.stop_frames&&!engine.external_audio`, after ~1200ms; therefore **a user editing during a long-running song then switching off cannot rely on it being saved**. This is a plausible root cause; verify on device/host rather than treating it as proven.
- `device/app.c` UI edit `control==38` currently uses binary `visual_mode=d>0`; update to 0–2 (same migration requirement as #36), with explicit navigation and readback.
- `device/arrangement.c` currently restores `visual_mode` on bank load; decide/document global-vs-bank precedence and test.

### Performance/flash safety
- No blocking flash write on audio real-time interrupt or long, audible XRUN-causing UI stall. Implement reliable, coalesced, wear-conscious and crash/power-loss-safe global settings storage consistent with FM-1 platform APIs; don't continuously write every knob tick. If the underlying platform cannot safely persist while playing, explicitly surface a reliable way to commit before power off and report limitation instead of falsely claiming persistence. Preserve v0.6.6 real-time smoothness.
- Verify power-cycle (not just app in-memory reinit), changing Mode 1→2→3 while PLAY, reboot after bounded idle, saved bank LOAD, fallback from malformed settings, 0.6.5/0.6.6 migration and direct updater, no false bank corruption, and 240×240 UI readback. Owner physical confirmation remains separate.

**Next-build required**, not part of published v0.6.6 acceptance. Preserve v0.6.6/source and backups; do not start a competing builder. Both performance MIDI transports remain deferred; KIRA-9 untouched.

title: P0 next AQUORA: Intention + music-style drum/mixer/FX profiles; fresh reboot defaults, reapply on every selection
body:
## Owner FM-1 behavior request — next AQUORA release (2026-11-07)

> "on reboot drums reset to default values, but when you select an intention it should be selecting its own drum kit, drum settings, delay, pan, fx send, presence etc... everytime a intention is selected and based on that intention/music style."

### Required contract — default on boot, intelligent on intention/style choice
1. **Fresh power-on without intentional bank recall:** Start with reliable, documented standard/default drum values, rather than accidentally carrying the last session's modified drum density, kit, hit, presence, pan or sends into a new song. Global preference memory (#39) must **not** quietly persist live musical parameters.
2. **Every explicit intention selection:** Apply a musically coherent **intention + music style** sound profile. Includes drum-kit choice, drum on/off policy if applicable, density, HIT/transient strength, drum level, **drum presence**, groove/accent/feel and appropriate drum channel **PAN** and **FX SEND**, along with **delay** and other relevant music FX settings (e.g., reverb/space) and sound palette/nature consistency. Do not simply keep the previous intention's pan/FX send/presence. Different intentions/modes should result in meaningfully different, balanced, recognizable profiles, not universal identical defaults or arbitrary all-max settings.
3. **Music style changes:** Standard, Cinematic and Neoclassical styles should re-evaluate the current intention's entire associated rhythm, mixer and FX profile automatically, without requiring New Song, Reroll or reboot. Style and intention must jointly determine coherent defaults.
4. **Re-select current intention:** Treat a deliberate user re-selection as a request to refresh/reapply that intention/style profile (potentially with tasteful seeded variation) rather than silently ignoring it; avoid triggers from ordinary frame redraw/reboot initialization.
5. **Manual controls and explicit locks:** On **unlocked/automatic** fields, intention/style selection is authoritative and re-applies profile values. A deliberate user lock/override should be respected where that policy is intentionally exposed, with a clear on-screen indicator and easy Auto/Reset action. Do not let hidden stale locks prevent a new intention/style from changing drums and FX. State which settings are auto-managed vs locked and don't silently retain old values.
6. **Transitions:** When PLAY is running, update rhythm/kit/FX/pan/send values at safe musical boundaries with bounded smoothing/crossfade and no clicks, reverb tail chopping, stuck tones, jumps, CPU spikes or XRUNs. Keep intensity suitable for sound-healing ambience; preserve punchiness, kit clarity and space. If any parameter cannot change atomically mid-PLAY, queue it visibly for the next safe phrase/bar.
7. **Arrangement banks:** Four Save Banks intentionally restore stored song-specific drum/mixer/FX states. A bank recall is distinct from fresh boot defaults and explicit subsequent intention/style selection. Normal reboot should not load all previous live tweak values into a fresh session by accident. Keep Reroll Sounds/lock/motif behavior and New Song semantics consistent.

### Source findings — v0.6.6 (avoid rebuilding what already works)
- `device/dsp/engine.c::apply_sound_profile` already has 13 intention palettes for weighted kit choice/density/hit and style-specific reverb/delay; no need to rewrite from scratch.
- However, the profile does not explicitly cover the current `engine.drum_presence`, `engine.drum_level`, `engine.tracks[SR_DRUMS].pan`, `engine.tracks[SR_DRUMS].send` (or relevant kit-sensitive rhythm mix dynamics). These may therefore remain stale across explicit intention changes.
- `sr_set_scene` applies the profile only when `changed=scene!=e->scene||!e->song_seed`; selecting the already selected intention currently only calls Nature selection, so it needs an explicit selection/refresh path without resetting randomly in ordinary playback.
- `sr_set_music_mode` forces a new scene realization; retain the good behavior and extend to all profile parameters.
- On boot `sr_init` initializes drums to `kit=0`, density 2, hit 25, presence 50, level .66, but `app_init` subsequently generates a new song and applies the scene palette. Make startup rules explicit and acceptance-test their expected state.

Replace with more legible musical reaction: multiple keyed/group pulses from actual voice/drum events, stronger hold/release (~short but visible; profile safely), rhythmic clusters/evolution, changing note accents and perceptually ~2.5x more action. title: P0 next AQUORA: Make 16/32/64-step loops musically distinct—true multi-bar phrases, harmonies, bass/drum development
body:
## Owner physical FM-1 test — AQUORA v0.6.6 (2026-11-07)
> "change from 16, to 32 or 64 should be more useful... right now i cannot really notice it doing anything... the patterns usually remain the same regardless, lets look into it."

**P0 musical-functionality quality gap**: 16/32/64 LOOP STEPS should produce audibly and meaningfully different phrase architectures, not merely altered loop-wrap/evolution timing or slight variation of one 16-step idea.

### Source-based diagnosis (v0.6.6 `aquora-next-integration`)
- `device/dsp/serenity.h` stores only `melody[16]` and `motif_home[16]`, irrespective of `loop_length`.
- `device/dsp/engine.c::motif_degree(e,step)` indexes `melody[step & 15]`, with a small bar-based pitch-degree transform for second/further bars. This cannot independently compose full 32-/64-step call/answer sections on its own.
- `trigger` builds `idx=loop_pos`, sets `s=idx` for 32/64 but uses **absolute step** for 16. This creates counterintuitive differences: multi-loop 16 can continue bar-dependent progression while longer lengths wrap `s` within their block; for many step gates/events `s & 15` stays identical on each bar. Different wrap timing alone is not enough audible distinction.
- `drum_trigger` and other role note gates use `step&15`; higher bars only have minor additions/accents. `mode_phrase` uses a four-slot progression but insufficient shared per-bar compositional contrast. The existing macro-role system (#34) has independently probability-gated roles rather than planning intentional complementary bar/section functions.
- `sr_set_loop_length` queues a new length until a loop boundary while playing. This is safe but can make the control feel unresponsive. The UI labels `NEXT LOOP STEPS` but a short, clear pending/applied indication and audible preview transition would improve understanding.
- Existing `tests/role_evolution_next.c` (117 scenario combinations) checks role targets, nonquiet role stems and fades; `tests/arrangement_roles_060.c` checks correct iteration counts, long scheduling and role event presence. **Neither establishes a perceptible distinct musical structure between same-seed 16,32,64**, so the owner's observation remains valid despite tests passing.

### Musical specifications by loop length
1. **16 — motif/groove:** one concise repeatable rhythmic/harmonic idea, coherent and suitable for steady meditation, with optional subtle fills and low-rate evolution; preserve current recognizable core motif as appropriate.
2. **32 — two-bar phrase:** deliberate first-bar statement and **second-bar answer/development**: differentiated lead/harmony contours, alternating bass movement, chord/pad voicings, tasteful drum answer/fills and short phrase resolutions. The second half must not be a simply transposed carbon copy of the first.
3. **64 — four-bar passage:** coherent **A / A′ / B / resolution (or intention/style-appropriate alternative)** with more distinct melodic development, bass progression, sustained textures/choir motion, varied percussion articulation, intentional accompaniment entrances and closing fill. Avoid arbitrary dense chaos or forcing all eight roles to sound simultaneously.
4. **All 13 intentions × 3 music styles:** the level/pace of contrast must reflect the intention and style. Some can be minimal and spacious, others more expansive, but **every longer setting needs noticeable multi-bar identity**. Preserve correct scale/tonic, exact reference Hz, binaural separation, smooth texture changes, FX/Nature behavior and human listening serenity.
5. **Musical form above loop length:** distinguish **pattern length** (how many steps a phrase spans) from **macro sections** (arrival/bloom/rest/breakdown/return) and **EVOLVE PACE/VARIATION** (how often and strongly themes transform). Work with #34 macro song-form improvement so drums don't randomly fade simply due to a role coin toss. Maintain stable motif memory and tasteful return.
6. **Switching while PLAY:** length update at next safe boundary with visible current vs pending value; preserve musical continuity (no unexpected motif reset/stuck notes/FX cuts), change actually audible in the next matching phrase, obey STOP/freeze and explicitly saved banks. Add small contextual "1 phrase / 2 phrases / 4 phrases" labels if possible without UI clutter.
7. **Implementation:** design compact, original, deterministic, seed-stable per-bar phrase variations / response and harmonic-state plans; avoid expensive real-time generation, RAM/flash bloat or copying SIREN GPL code/assets. Reuse existing 16-step motif memory as source material but add a proper higher-level plan for 32/64, with graceful solo/mute and sound locks.

### Mandatory evidence and acceptance
- Controlled **same seed, intention, music mode, instruments, variation level** A/B/C recordings for 16/32/64, preferably isolated stems + full mix and score/event timelines. Compare distinct melodic note-degree sequences, bass/chord changes, drum hit maps and onset/gain per bar. Assert **meaningful musical sequence differences and higher-order development**, not just that role events exist or step counts differ. Keep music coherent; don't assert a fixed Hamming distance without listening context.
- Tests 13 intentions × 3 music modes × 3 lengths with variation 0/Stable and flowing/high, freeze, save/recall, returning motif, pending length changes while playing, New Song/Reroll, long sessions with section return; verify deterministic plan and click-free transitions.
- Full native + forced single core + emulator and hardware acceptance checklist; preserve v0.6.6 smoothness, screen performance/headroom, no XRUN regressions. Owner will physically judge whether longer lengths sound unmistakably richer.

**Status:** owner-observed v0.6.6 behavior / required next corrective build. Do not modify existing release, overwrite checkpoints, start overlapping Work sessions, or touch KIRA-9. Both performance MIDI transports remain deferred.

Related #9 EVOLVE, #34 SIREN-inspired macro form and intentional drum fades, #40 intention/style profile, #32 single requirements matrix.
